suggestions: Apply temporal smoothing to the composite score before cross-sectional ranking, e.g. Rank(Ma((Pct(vwap,10)+(Sum((volume*Greater(close,vwap)),10)/Sum(volume,10))),5),40). VWAP drift and above-VWAP accumulation are medium-term flow patterns; ranking the raw 10-day composite daily makes rank order hypersensitive to one-day window roll-offs and marginal VWAP prints. A short moving average of the composite preserves the economic thesis while filtering high-frequency rank reshuffles that drive the 71% realized turnover without requiring a longer investment horizon.

Require multi-horizon persistence by averaging 10-day and 20-day versions of both legs before the final Rank, e.g. Rank(((Pct(vwap,10)+Pct(vwap,20))/2 + ((Sum((volume*Greater(close,vwap)),10)/Sum(volume,10))+(Sum((volume*Greater(close,vwap)),20)/Sum(volume,20)))/2),40). Single-horizon windows let names enter and exit the top bucket on transient spikes that reverse once the window rolls forward, producing churn without durable sponsorship. Blending horizons keeps only names with sustained VWAP trend and accumulation, which tend to hold rank longer and reduce daily portfolio rotation.

Replace endpoint VWAP return with volatility-normalized trend strength, e.g. Rank((Pct(vwap,10)/Stdev(Pct(vwap,1),10)+(Sum((volume*Greater(close,vwap)),10)/Sum(volume,10))),40). Raw percentage change ranks volatile tickers aggressively even when their VWAP path is noisy mean-reversion around the anchor; these names oscillate across quintiles as daily noise dominates signal. Scaling momentum by recent VWAP return volatility down-weights whipsaw candidates and stabilizes cross-sectional ordering, lowering turnover while keeping directionally trending, institutionally supported names at the top.
